standardOfCare.setting: Mastectomy or breast-conserving surgery, and when to reconstruct
standardOfCare.approach: Breast-conserving surgery (wide local excision) followed by radiotherapy is usually as effective as mastectomy (Macmillan); mastectomy is advised when the cancer is large compared with the breast, there are several areas of cancer, or after earlier chest radiotherapy, and some people choose it. Chemotherapy first often makes conservation possible. Cancer at the margin means further surgery (NICE NG101: re-excise at 0 mm, consider within 1 mm). NICE says offer reconstruction to everyone having a mastectomy, offer both immediate and delayed options whether or not they are available locally, and offer immediate reconstruction even to those who may need radiotherapy; its table lists the trade-offs (implants more affected by radiotherapy than flaps; complications can delay chemotherapy or radiotherapy; more time to decide with delayed reconstruction). Some people prefer no reconstruction. The armpit is staged with a sentinel node biopsy (1 to 3 nodes); removing all the nodes raises the risk of lymphoedema and is reserved for involved nodes that need clearing.

guideline.version: NICE NG101, sections 1.4 and 1.5 (2018 to 2024); Macmillan and Cancer Research UK surgery pages

standardOfCare.setting: Radiotherapy after surgery: which schedule and where
standardOfCare.approach: After breast-conserving surgery the remaining breast is treated; after mastectomy the chest wall is treated when nodes were involved (macrometastases) or margins were involved, including after neoadjuvant chemotherapy where pretreatment tests showed involved nodes, and considered for node-negative T3 disease. NICE NG101 (2023): offer 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week when the lymph nodes are not being treated (FAST-Forward: non-inferior to 40 Gy in 15 at 5 years), consider 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks after implant reconstruction or where 3 weeks suits better, and offer 40 Gy in 15 fractions whenever regional nodes are irradiated (START-B). A boost to the tumour bed is offered where the risk of local recurrence is high. Partial-breast radiotherapy (IMPORT LOW) is reserved for low-risk ER-positive tumours in NICE's wording, so it rarely applies to triple-negative disease. Left-sided treatment often uses breath-hold to protect the heart. Skin reactions peak at the end and settle over 3 to 4 weeks.

guideline.version: NICE NG101, section 1.13 (2023); FAST-Forward (Lancet 2020); START (Lancet Oncology 2013)

standardOfCare.setting: Fertility preservation before chemotherapy
standardOfCare.approach: Triple-negative breast cancer is more common under 40 and chemotherapy usually starts within weeks. NICE NG101 asks teams to advise everyone about options for preserving fertility and cross-refers to the NICE fertility guideline; Cancer Research UK says national guidelines expect the discussion at diagnosis. Options: embryo or egg freezing (about 2 to 3 weeks of ovarian stimulation, with random-start protocols to avoid delay), ovarian tissue freezing at a growing number of UK centres, and contraception during treatment because chemotherapy can damage eggs. NHS funding for freezing varies by area. Because this cancer has no hormone receptors there is no endocrine therapy to interrupt later; the question is protecting eggs before the first cycle, and asking early enough that the referral does not delay chemotherapy.

guideline.version: NICE NG101 recommendation 1.1.5 and NICE CG156 (fertility problems); Cancer Research UK and Macmillan fertility pages

standardOfCare.setting: Genetic testing and what a BRCA result means for your family
standardOfCare.approach: NICE NG101 says offer BRCA1 and BRCA2 testing to women under 50 with triple-negative breast cancer even with no family history; Breast Cancer Now says anyone diagnosed under 60 should be offered a referral to discuss testing, and the NHS test directory criteria that NICE points to for PARP inhibitor eligibility (R444.1) may make people over 60 eligible too. Testing is free on the NHS when a hospital specialist refers you, results take about 1 to 3 months, and a genetic counsellor helps with what the result means. A pathogenic variant: opens olaparib after chemotherapy for residual disease (NICE TA886) and a PARP inhibitor in metastatic disease; raises the question of risk-reducing surgery to the other breast and the ovaries, managed by a multidisciplinary team with counselling first (NICE CG164); and means each child has a 1 in 2 chance of carrying it, so relatives can be offered predictive testing. A variant of uncertain significance changes nothing yet. No variant found means relatives are not tested, though a strong family history may still raise risk.

guideline.version: NICE NG101 recommendation 1.3.6 (2017); NICE CG164; Breast Cancer Now genetic testing page

standardOfCare.setting: First treatment for metastatic disease: the tests that decide
standardOfCare.approach: Three results decide the first treatment for cancer that has spread, so ask that all three are back before the choice is made, ideally on a fresh biopsy because receptors can change: PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS 10 or more opens pembrolizumab with chemotherapy, NICE TA801, or with sacituzumab govitecan), germline BRCA status (a PARP inhibitor, olaparib or talazoparib), and HER2 score (1+ or 2+ without amplification, HER2-low, opens trastuzumab deruxtecan after chemotherapy). The TROP2 antibody-drug conjugates sacituzumab govitecan and datopotamab deruxtecan were approved first line in 2026 with different side-effect profiles; NHS funding follows NICE appraisals (sacituzumab govitecan is funded after two prior therapies under TA819), so ask what applies where you are treated. Ask for the palliative care team from the start, and think about a trial before the first line, because eligibility narrows with each treatment.

guideline.version: NICE TA801 (2022) and TA819 (2022); KEYNOTE-355 (NEJM 2022); NCCN Guidelines: Breast Cancer

standardOfCare.setting: Antibody-drug conjugates: what to expect and the side effects to report
standardOfCare.approach: An antibody-drug conjugate carries chemotherapy into cells that show its target (TROP2 for sacituzumab govitecan and datopotamab deruxtecan, HER2 for trastuzumab deruxtecan), given as a drip in cycles: sacituzumab govitecan on days 1 and 8 of 21. The effects are still chemotherapy-like. Sacituzumab govitecan: low white cells (boxed warning; growth factor injections are sometimes used) and diarrhoea (boxed warning; Macmillan's rule is ring the 24-hour line for 4 or more stools a day, stools at night, or anti-diarrhoea medicine not working within 24 hours), plus sickness, tiredness and hair loss. Datopotamab deruxtecan: mouth soreness, eye problems (the label requires eye examinations) and rarely lung inflammation. Trastuzumab deruxtecan: interstitial lung disease in about 15% (2.2% fatal in the pooled analysis), mostly in the first year, so any new cough, breathlessness or fever is reported immediately; also sickness and low counts. Blood tests before each dose; doses are delayed or reduced rather than pushed through.

guideline.version: NICE TA819 (2022); ASCENT (NEJM 2021); US prescribing information (Trodelvy, Datroway, Enhertu); Macmillan and Breast Cancer Now drug pages

standardOfCare.setting: Brain metastases: radiosurgery, whole-brain radiotherapy, surgery and drugs
standardOfCare.approach: Triple-negative breast cancer spreads to the brain more often than other breast subtypes: about 29% of people with metastatic disease in a 433-patient series (25% within two years), and 46% before death in an older 116-patient series. For 1 to 3 metastases of a size suitable for radiosurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery alone is generally preferred: in a randomised trial it caused less cognitive decline at 3 months than radiosurgery plus whole-brain radiotherapy (63.5% against 91.7%) with no difference in survival. Whole-brain radiotherapy is kept for many or widespread metastases, with hippocampal-sparing planning and memantine where possible. Surgery is considered for a single large metastasis causing pressure. Drug treatment for the rest of the body usually continues; activity of the antibody-drug conjugates in the brain is emerging but unproven (the palliation term carries the ASCENT, real-world and DEBBRAH figures). Steroids relieve swelling in the short term. Ask what the plan is for symptoms (headache, seizures, weakness) and who to ring.

guideline.version: Brown et al., NCCTG N0574 (JAMA 2016); NCCN Guidelines: Central Nervous System Cancers

standardOfCare.setting: A clinical trial or standard treatment
standardOfCare.approach: At every stage a trial can be a reasonable choice beside standard treatment: ask what the comparison arm is, whether a placebo is used (the NHS says only where no proven treatment exists; in KEYNOTE-522 the control arm had chemotherapy plus placebo, never placebo alone), what extra visits, tests and travel are involved and whether travel is paid, and that you can leave at any time without it affecting your care. Trials open to triple-negative breast cancer include ones testing less treatment after a complete response (OptimICE-pCR), anthracycline-free chemotherapy (SCARLET), circulating tumour DNA-guided escalation, and new antibody-drug conjugates in metastatic disease; the Triple Negative Breast Cancer Foundation and Cancer Research UK run trial finders. NICE NG101 asks teams to discuss research opportunities and encourage trial entry.

guideline.version: NICE NG101 recommendation 1.1.4 (discuss research opportunities and encourage trial entry); NHS: clinical trials

standardOfCare.setting: Choice of neoadjuvant backbone: the platinum debate
standardOfCare.approach: Carboplatin raises pathological complete response in every trial (GeparSixto 53.2 versus 36.9 percent, BrighTNess 58 versus 31, CALGB 40603) and improved disease-free survival in GeparSixto (hazard ratio 0.56) and event-free survival in BrighTNess (0.57) but not long-term outcomes in CALGB 40603 (not powered); it is part of the KEYNOTE-522 regimen and is standard in the UK. Adding veliparib to carboplatin added nothing (BrighTNess). Atezolizumab in place of pembrolizumab has no survival evidence (NeoTRIP, GeparDouze, ALEXANDRA).

guideline.version: ESMO early breast cancer guideline 2024

standardOfCare.setting: Germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers: early-stage choices
standardOfCare.approach: About one in nine unselected triple-negative patients carries a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant (11.2 percent, Couch 2015; 15.4 percent in a prospective registry, Sharma 2014; 17.2 percent in GeparSixto, Hahnen 2017); the testing rules are in the germline testing row. The result decides adjuvant olaparib (OlympiA, 82 percent triple-negative; NICE TA886), informs risk-reducing surgery, and in the UK offers PARTNER (olaparib with neoadjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel, 30 sites). Platinum sensitivity is greatest in carriers (TNT: response 68 versus 33 percent with carboplatin versus docetaxel in metastatic disease).

guideline.version: NICE TA886 (2023); NCCN Breast Cancer

standardOfCare.setting: Metastatic, germline BRCA1 or BRCA2
standardOfCare.approach: Olaparib (OlympiAD: progression-free survival 7.0 versus 4.2 months, hazard ratio 0.58; no overall survival gain overall, hazard ratio 0.51 in patients untreated for metastatic disease; NICE TA1040) or talazoparib (EMBRACA: 8.6 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.54; final overall survival hazard ratio 0.85; NICE TA952), with the lower-cost option first in England; a platinum doublet is the alternative (BROCADE3 control arm median survival 28.2 months); PARP inhibitor added to chemotherapy (veliparib, BROCADE3) improved progression-free but not overall survival and is not licensed. Sequence relative to PD-1 or TROP2 ADC first-line therapy is untested.

guideline.version: NICE TA1040 (2025), TA952 (2024); ESMO metastatic breast cancer guideline 2021

standardOfCare.setting: Metastatic, HER2-low, after one or two lines of chemotherapy
standardOfCare.approach: Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks (DESTINY-Breast04: overall survival 23.4 versus 16.8 months in all patients, hazard ratio 0.64; hormone-receptor-negative cohort of 63, progression-free survival 8.5 versus 2.9 months, hazard ratio 0.46; interstitial lung disease 12.1 percent, 0.8 percent fatal). Licensed in the US (2022) and EU (2023) for HER2-low regardless of hormone receptor status; in England NICE first said no (TA992, 29 July 2024), then recommended it after chemotherapy in the metastatic setting or early recurrence after adjuvant chemotherapy (TA1197, 7 October 2026, replacing TA992), funded through the Cancer Drugs Fund until routine commissioning begins. HER2-ultralow triple-negative disease has no licensed indication.

guideline.version: NICE TA1197 (October 2026, recommended; replaces TA992); ESMO metastatic breast cancer guideline 2021

standardOfCare.setting: Palliation of symptoms: bone, pleura, skin and end of life
standardOfCare.approach: Single-fraction radiotherapy for painful bone metastases with denosumab or zoledronic acid to reduce skeletal events; urgent radiotherapy or surgery for spinal cord compression; drainage with talc pleurodesis or an indwelling catheter for malignant pleural effusion; radiotherapy and wound care for chest wall recurrence; management of drug toxicities (hand-foot syndrome on capecitabine, neutropenia and diarrhoea on sacituzumab govitecan, stomatitis and eye symptoms on datopotamab deruxtecan, interstitial lung disease on trastuzumab deruxtecan); early integrated palliative care from diagnosis of metastatic disease.

guideline.version: ESMO metastatic breast cancer guideline 2021

stateOfArt: Curative-intent: chemo-immunotherapy (KEYNOTE-522) cures more patients than ever; pCR ~65%. Adjuvant PARP inhibitor for BRCA carriers.

Metastatic: ADCs first line (sacituzumab, Dato-DXd), ADC + IO for PD-L1+ disease; median OS in first-line trials now approaches two years (23.0 months with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy at CPS 10 or more in KEYNOTE-355), against 13.3 months in a 2000 to 2006 series.
HER2-low staining can meet one condition of a specified advanced-breast-cancer T-DXd use; stage, prior treatment and the full indication still govern eligibility.
De-escalation is real: TIL-guided omission of chemotherapy in stage I; anthracycline-free and pembrolizumab-omission trials in stage II-III.

Genomic landscape. TP53 mutation in about 80% (79 to 90% by cohort), PIK3CA 10 to 18%, PTEN loss 12 to 35%, RB1 loss 15 to 20%, MYC amplification 18 to 35%, EGFR amplification 3 to 6%, NOTCH activation 5 to 9%, PI3K-AKT pathway alteration 20 to 27%; germline BRCA1 7 to 11%, BRCA2 3 to 4%, PALB2 1 to 2%, and homologous recombination deficiency in 59 to 71% (mostly BRCA1 promoter methylation and sporadic scars rather than germline mutation). TMB 10 or more in 4 to 5% of early and 18% of pretreated metastatic disease; MSI-high 0 to 2%. Every figure and cohort is in the molecular table; the cBioPortal rows were computed on receptor-defined triple-negative subsets of TCGA, METABRIC and the MSK 2018 cohort.

Subtypes. Lehmann's TNBCtype-4: BL1 35% (TP53 92%, unstable, platinum-sensitive, pCR 41%), BL2 22% (growth-factor signalling, pCR 18%), mesenchymal 25% (EMT, immune-cold, PRC2-silenced MHC-I, lung-tropic) and LAR 16% (AR-driven, PIK3CA 55%, AKT1 13%, bone-tropic, pCR 29%, worst prognosis, modest AR-antagonist benefit); the immunomodulatory signal (21 to 25%) is the lymphocyte infiltrate and carries the best prognosis. Burstein's BLIS and BLIA split basal-like disease by immune state; the FUSCC scheme repeats the four-way logic in 465 Chinese patients. By PAM50, 76% of TNBC is basal-like and 15% HER2-enriched.

Immune biomarkers by assay. SP142 IC 1% or more (IMpassion130): 41 to 51%. 22C3 CPS 10 or more (KEYNOTE-355, ASCENT-04): 27 to 38%. The two agree weakly and are not interchangeable; a 22C3 or SP263 positive does not imply SP142 positivity, and the atezolizumab benefit sat in SP142-positive tumours. Stromal TILs average 23%, are 60% or more in about 30%, and predict chemotherapy response and survival with or without chemotherapy; spatial immune classes (immunoreactive, immune-cold B7-H4-high, stroma-restricted) refine the score.

HER2 and TROP2. HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-negative) is 24 to 37% of TNBC and on-label for trastuzumab deruxtecan after one line (DESTINY-Breast04, 63 hormone receptor-negative patients); ultralow is a further 38% but unlabelled in TNBC because DESTINY-Breast06 was hormone receptor-positive only. TROP2 is not tested: ASCENT benefit spanned high and medium H-scores and neither TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate requires an assay.

Ancestry and geography. African ancestry carries a 3.8-fold odds of basal-like disease, more TP53 and fewer PIK3CA mutations, an estimated heritability of 0.44 for basal versus non-basal subtype and a distinct immune landscape; 46% of Nigerian breast cancers with receptor data are triple-negative and 14.7% carry a germline repair-gene variant. BRCA1 founder mutations dominate in the Bahamas (23% of unselected patients), Mexico (ex9-12del) and Ashkenazi Jews (185delAG); Chinese TNBC carries more PIK3CA; MSI-high is under 1% in China and Japan.

ctDNA and molecular residual disease. Post-neoadjuvant ctDNA positivity (about a third of patients with residual disease, rising with residual cancer burden) carries a two- to four-fold relapse hazard independent of RCB; every pathological complete responder in I-SPY 2 was ctDNA-negative. Prospective surveillance (c-TRAK TN) found ctDNA in 27% by a year but most already had metastases and pembrolizumab cleared none, and brain-only relapse escapes detection. No TNBC approval uses ctDNA; it stratifies ASCENT-05 and the ZEST design.

Testing. Germline BRCA1/2 (and PALB2) for every TNBC diagnosis (ASCO-SSO 2024; NHS R208 and R444.1), with results before surgery where possible; 22C3 CPS on a metastatic biopsy for pembrolizumab combinations; HER2 IHC re-read at the 0 versus 1+ boundary; a comprehensive tumour panel at relapse for TMB, MSI, PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN and NOTCH; HRD scores and TROP2 IHC are research readouts with no breast label.

history.title: HER2 amplification found in 30 percent of breast cancers and tied to early relapse
history.note: Slamon and colleagues, 189 tumours. With the oestrogen and progesterone receptor assays it completed the three tests whose absence defines triple-negative disease.

history.title: Founder BRCA mutations: 56 percent breast cancer risk by 70 in Ashkenazi carriers
history.note: Struewing and colleagues, 5,318 volunteers, three founder variants carried by over 2 percent of the population; Górski described the Polish BRCA1 founder set in 2000.

history.title: Molecular portraits define the basal-like subtype
history.note: Perou and Sørlie's expression profiling separates basal-like from luminal breast cancers.

history.title: BRCA1 carriers' tumours shown to be basal-like
history.note: Sørlie's independent data sets and Foulkes's cytokeratin 5/6 stain (odds ratio 9.0) linked hereditary and basal-like disease; Atchley (2008) found 57 percent of BRCA1 carriers' cancers triple-negative.

history.title: Carolina Breast Cancer Study: basal-like tumours in 39 percent of young African American women
history.note: Carey and colleagues, 496 cases; 16 percent in other women. California registry data (2007) fixed the wider demography of younger, Black, Hispanic and poorer women with worse survival at every stage.

history.title: 'Triple-negative' enters clinical vocabulary
history.note: Defined by negative ER, PR and HER2 test classifications; recognised as a subtype with limited treatment options, which helped set the research agenda that followed.

history.title: Residual cancer burden score; the relapse curve that peaks at three years
history.note: Symmans graded residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy; Dent's Toronto cohort showed distant relapse hazard ratio 2.6 peaking at three years and fading after five.

history.title: The residual disease paradox and the brain metastasis rate
history.note: Liedtke: pathological complete response 22 vs 11 percent yet worse survival, driven by residual disease. Lin: 46 percent of metastatic patients developed brain metastases; median survival 13.3 months.

history.title: Claudin-low described as a breast cancer subtype
history.note: Mostly triple-negative tumours with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and stem-cell features (Prat, Breast Cancer Research); re-defined as a phenotype across subtypes in 2020.

history.title: Six molecular subtypes of triple-negative breast cancer
history.note: Lehmann and colleagues, 587 tumours: basal-like 1 and 2, immunomodulatory, mesenchymal, mesenchymal stem-like, luminal androgen receptor; refined to four in 2016 (Burstein reached a similar four in 2015).

history.title: TCGA basal-like portrait and the first TNBC genomes
history.note: TP53 80%, PTEN loss 35%, RB1 loss 20% in basal-like disease and a likeness to serous ovarian cancer (Nature); Shah's 104 TNBC genomes show a continuous spectrum of clonal complexity.

history.title: Carboplatin raises pCR
history.note: GeparSixto and CALGB 40603 show platinum increases pathologic complete response.

history.title: UK POSH cohort: young Black women have more triple-negative disease and worse survival despite equal access
history.note: Copson and colleagues, 2,915 women aged 40 or under: 26.1 vs 18.6 percent triple-negative; five-year survival 71.1 vs 82.4 percent with equal chemotherapy use.

history.title: Germline testing case made for all triple-negative disease
history.note: 14.6 percent of 1,824 unselected triple-negative patients carry a predisposition mutation, 11.2 percent in BRCA1 or BRCA2 (Couch, JCO); the same year Burstein's basal-like immunosuppressed and immune-activated subtypes split basal-like disease by immune state.

history.title: TNBCtype-4 and the HRD score threshold
history.note: Lehmann refines the subtypes to four (BL1 35%, BL2 22%, M 25%, LAR 16%) with pCR 41% versus 18% versus 29%; Telli sets HRD score 42 in neoadjuvant platinum trials.

history.title: AJCC 8th edition adds the prognostic stage
history.note: Grade, ER, PR and HER2 enter the stage group alongside TNM (Giuliano, CA); validated in 2018.

history.title: CREATE-X: capecitabine after residual disease lengthens survival
history.note: 910 patients; five-year overall survival 89.2 vs 83.6 percent, and 78.8 vs 70.3 percent in the triple-negative group. The first post-neoadjuvant treatment.

history.title: First immunotherapy signal
history.note: IMpassion130: atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel improves PFS in PD-L1+ metastatic TNBC (approval later withdrawn).

history.title: PARP inhibitors in BRCA breast cancer
history.note: OlympiAD and EMBRACA lead to olaparib and talazoparib approvals.

history.title: TNT: germline BRCA, not the HRD score, predicts platinum benefit
history.note: In 376 advanced patients carboplatin doubled the response rate in germline BRCA carriers while the Myriad HRD score and BRCA1 methylation predicted nothing; Bareche maps mutations onto the Lehmann subtypes in 550 tumours.

history.title: WHO classification of breast tumours, 5th edition
history.note: Medullary carcinoma becomes a pattern of invasive carcinoma of no special type; metaplastic, adenoid cystic, apocrine and secretory carcinomas keep their special-type status.

history.title: Population whole genomes and TILs
history.note: SCAN-B whole-genome sequencing puts HRDetect-high at 59% of TNBC (Nat Med); Loi's pooled 2,148 patients fix TILs as the strongest early prognostic marker.

history.title: Sacituzumab govitecan approved
history.note: ASCENT: OS 12.1 vs 6.7 months in pretreated disease; first ADC for TNBC.

history.title: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy first line
history.note: KEYNOTE-355 in CPS ≥10 disease.

history.title: ASCO/CAP creates the ER Low Positive category
history.note: ER 1 to 10 percent is reported as ER Low Positive, with limited endocrine-benefit evidence and recognition of biological heterogeneity. Similar outcomes in selected observational cohorts do not erase that classification.

history.title: Post-neoadjuvant ctDNA triples the relapse hazard
history.note: BRE12-158's preplanned analysis of 196 residual-disease patients: distant relapse hazard ratio 2.99 and death hazard ratio 4.16 when ctDNA is detected after chemotherapy.

history.title: KEYNOTE-522 changes early-stage care
history.note: Neoadjuvant/adjuvant pembrolizumab approved for stage II-III TNBC; OS benefit confirmed 2024.

history.title: OlympiA: adjuvant olaparib
history.note: One year of olaparib after standard therapy improves iDFS and OS in gBRCA carriers.

history.title: PD-L1 assays shown not to be interchangeable
history.note: Rugo and colleagues on 614 IMpassion130 tumours: SP142, SP263 and 22C3 positive in 46, 75 and 73 percent, concordance 69 percent. Atezolizumab's US breast indication withdrawn the same year.

history.title: HER2-low measured at about a third of TNBC
history.note: Schettini (3,689 HER2-negative cancers, 36.6% of triple-negative) and Denkert (34.0% of 1,162 hormone receptor-negative trial patients) fix the share a year before DESTINY-Breast04 gave it a drug.

history.title: HER2-low: T-DXd works in 'HER2-negative' disease
history.note: DESTINY-Breast04 includes TNBC patients with HER2-low tumours.

history.title: African ancestry linked to the TNBC immune landscape
history.note: Martini's RNA sequencing of African American, West and East African tumours finds 613 ancestry-associated genes and distinct tumour-associated immune profiles.

history.title: c-TRAK TN: acting on ctDNA came too late
history.note: UK trial, 161 women under surveillance; 27 percent ctDNA-positive by a year, 72 percent of them already metastatic on staging; none of five given pembrolizumab cleared.

history.title: ctDNA and residual cancer burden shown independently prognostic
history.note: Stecklein's 80-patient registry: ctDNA positive in a third of residual-disease patients, rising with RCB class, with three-year event-free survival 48% against 82%.

history.title: Lymphocyte-rich stage I tumours do well without chemotherapy
history.note: Leon-Ferre and colleagues, 1,966 untreated patients: five-year distant recurrence-free survival 94 percent with lymphocytes of 50 percent or more vs 78 percent below 30 percent.

history.title: Universal germline testing recommended
history.note: ASCO-SSO recommends BRCA1/2 testing for all breast cancer diagnosed at 65 or under and for every PARP inhibitor candidate.

history.title: First-line ADC era begins
history.note: ASCENT-03, ASCENT-04, and TROPION-Breast02 all positive; TROPION-Breast02 shows OS benefit.

history.title: Bispecific ADC succeeds; first-line ADC approvals
history.note: Iza-bren phase 3 positive (Feb 2026); FDA approves Dato-DXd and sacituzumab govitecan first line (Q2 2026).

history.title: TROPION-Breast02 and OlympiA six-year update published; CAPItello-290 negative
history.note: Datopotamab deruxtecan first line: overall survival 23.7 vs 18.7 months. Olaparib: six-year survival 87.5 vs 83.2 percent, no excess leukaemia. Capivasertib plus paclitaxel: no survival gain.

history.title: HER2-ultralow share of TNBC measured
history.note: Boissiere-Michot reclassifies 367 untreated TNBCs as 38% null, 38% ultralow and 24% low, none prognostic; ultralow stays unlabelled in TNBC.

openProblems: Residual disease after KEYNOTE-522: no approved escalation beyond capecitabine/olaparib; ctDNA-guided trials needed.
ADC sequencing: does a second TOP1-payload ADC work after the first? SATEEN/BRE-354 suggest limited efficacy; chemotherapy interposition debated.
Patient selection for TROP2 ADCs: IHC does not predict; TROP2 PET and ctDNA are candidates.
PD-L1-negative early disease has immunotherapy proven only in KEYNOTE-522's unselected population, no biomarker that spares anyone pembrolizumab, and no ADC yet in the curative setting.
Brain metastases (up to 30-45% of metastatic TNBC) remain undertreated; ADC CNS activity is emerging but unproven.
Mesenchymal/claudin-low biology (EMT, efflux pumps) resists chemotherapy, ADC payloads, and immunotherapy alike.
Disparities: Black women have twice the TNBC incidence and worse outcomes; trial enrolment does not reflect this.

No UK registry publishes triple-negative incidence or survival as a subtype; the UK share rests on Cancer Research UK's around 15 percent and on cohorts such as POSH, while SEER publishes rates by receptor status every year.

The 2022 low-ER registry report noted exclusions from TNBC trials. Similar outcomes in selected cohorts treated similarly do not establish equivalence of all regimens or populations. Check the actual protocol and current treatment evidence for ER-low disease; test classification and study eligibility remain separate.

Chemoprevention for BRCA1 carriers: tamoxifen and anastrozole prevent ER-positive disease, which is not the cancer BRCA1 carriers mostly get; risk-reducing mastectomy and surveillance are the only proven options.

PD-L1 assays disagree on about a third of tumours (SP142 46 percent positive, 22C3 73 percent, concordance 69 percent in IMpassion130; 27 percent CPS 10 or more against 51 percent SP142-positive in the Swedish early cohort); only 22C3 combined positive score of 10 has an approved drug attached, laboratories are not harmonised, and no assay predicts benefit from the first-line antibody-drug conjugate plus pembrolizumab combinations.

Acting on ctDNA after residual disease failed once (c-TRAK TN: detection came after metastases were visible, and ctDNA misses brain-only relapse); the next design needs tumour-informed assays, a sample at surgery and an active drug, and has not been run.

The disparity is measured in the United States and was measured once in the UK (POSH, women under 41, recruited to 2008); NHS statistics do not report triple-negative outcomes by ethnicity, and women of African ancestry, who carry a distinct immune landscape, remain under-represented in the trials that set the biomarker thresholds.

Most homologous recombination deficiency in TNBC is not germline BRCA, yet the PARP inhibitor labels are germline-only and the HRD scores validated in ovarian cancer did not predict carboplatin benefit in advanced TNBC (TNT).

The Lehmann subtypes predict chemotherapy response retrospectively but no prospective subtype-directed trial has changed a guideline; the mesenchymal and LAR subtypes have no approved targeted therapy.

Capecitabine after residual disease (CREATE-X) was proven before pembrolizumab existed; no trial has tested it alongside adjuvant pembrolizumab, and the two ADC trials in that setting (ASCENT-05, TROPION-Breast03) will not report before 2027.

The independent contribution of adjuvant pembrolizumab is unknown: KEYNOTE-522 gave it before and after surgery, OptimICE-pCR asks whether it can be dropped after a complete response, and SWOG S1418 asks whether it helps after residual disease without prior immunotherapy.

Three atezolizumab phase 3 trials in early disease were negative or null while pembrolizumab succeeded; whether that is the drug, the PD-L1 rather than PD-1 target, the backbone or chance is unresolved, and it leaves PD-L1-negative early disease with immunotherapy proven only in KEYNOTE-522's unselected population.

In England HER2-low triple-negative disease waited until October 2026 for trastuzumab deruxtecan (NICE TA992 said no in 2024; TA1197 recommends it), the first-line ADC indications await appraisal, and atezolizumab remains commissioned on a licence the United States withdrew; the UK and US pathways for metastatic disease have diverged.

AKT inhibition failed twice in biomarker-selected metastatic disease (IPATunity130, CAPItello-290) despite positive phase 2 trials, so PIK3CA, AKT1 and PTEN alterations, present in a fifth to a quarter of tumours, are not actionable in triple-negative breast cancer today; PTEN loss may also mark immunotherapy resistance.

symptoms: A new lump or thickening in the breast or armpit; a change in the size, shape or feel of the breast; puckering, dimpling, a rash or redness of the skin; fluid from the nipple when not pregnant or breastfeeding; a nipple that turns in (Cancer Research UK). The symptoms are the same as for other breast cancers, but triple-negative tumours arrive younger, more often between screening rounds, and more often at a higher grade
Redness may look darker or reddish brown on brown or black skin (Cancer Research UK symptoms page)

Less often found by screening: 29 percent of triple-negative cancers against 48 percent of hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative cancers presented through an abnormal screening mammogram in US cancer centres (Lin 2012)

Referral rules: an unexplained breast lump at 30 or over, or nipple discharge, retraction or other change in one nipple at 50 or over, goes on the suspected cancer pathway; skin changes or an unexplained axillary lump at 30 or over should prompt the same consideration (NICE NG12 1.4)
diagnosis: One-stop breast clinic and triple assessment: examination, mammogram, ultrasound and a needle core or vacuum-assisted biopsy, with ultrasound and needle biopsy of any abnormal axillary node (Cancer Research UK)

ER, PR and HER2 are tested together on the biopsy at diagnosis by quality-assured immunohistochemistry and reported quantitatively (NICE NG101 1.3.1 to 1.3.4); results take about 2 to 4 weeks (Cancer Research UK)

Triple-negative denotes negative ER, PR and HER2 test classifications. ER and PR are below 1 percent nuclear staining; HER2 is interpreted using the applicable IHC/ISH algorithm. ER 1 to 10 percent is ER Low Positive, with limited endocrine-benefit evidence, and is not ER-negative under ASCO/CAP criteria. Negative classifications do not establish zero receptor molecules

Retain the HER2 IHC score and any required ISH result. The 2023 ASCO-CAP guideline distinguishes reporting from proof of a biological threshold; eligibility for a particular ADC also depends on its current label, disease setting and other requirements

Germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 testing is offered to women under 50 with triple-negative disease even without a family history (NICE NG101 1.3.6); the familial cancer guideline adds a 10 percent carrier-probability rule for everyone else (CG164)

Breast MRI only where the extent is unclear, the breasts are dense or the cancer is lobular (NG101 1.2); CT, bone scan or PET-CT for staging when the stage or symptoms call for it; CA 15-3 is not diagnostic (Cancer Research UK)
staging: TNM 8th edition. T1 is 2 cm or less (T1a to 0.5 cm, T1b to 1 cm, T1c to 2 cm), T2 over 2 to 5 cm, T3 over 5 cm, T4 into the chest wall or skin or inflammatory (Cancer Research UK)

Nodes: cN before treatment, pN after surgery; pN1 one to three axillary nodes, pN2 four to nine, pN3 ten or more or infraclavicular, supraclavicular or axillary plus internal mammary nodes (Cancer Research UK)
Stage 1 is T1 N0 (1B with micrometastases); stage 2 is T2 N0, T0 to T2 N1 or T3 N0; stage 3 is N2, T3 N1, T4 or N3; stage 4 is any spread beyond the regional nodes (Cancer Research UK)
The AJCC prognostic stage adds grade, ER, PR and HER2 to the TNM groups; a grade 3 triple-negative tumour is generally placed higher than its anatomic stage (Giuliano 2017; Weiss 2018)

After chemotherapy before surgery, the pathologist reports whether any invasive cancer is left (pathological complete response) and how much (residual cancer burden classes I to III), which predict relapse better than the starting stage in this subtype (Cortazar 2014; Symmans 2017)

prognosis.text: Population figures, quoted with their cohorts; none is a personal prognosis. United States (SEER 21, excluding Illinois, people diagnosed 2016 to 2022): five-year relative survival for hormone receptor-negative, HER2-negative breast cancer is 78.7 percent, against 95.8 percent for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease and 91.9 percent for all breast cancer; by stage it is 92.8 percent for localised, 68.3 percent for regional and 14.9 percent for distant disease (the same fact sheet). Four-year breast cancer-specific survival was 77.0 percent for the triple-negative subtype in SEER cases diagnosed 2010 to 2013 (Howlader 2018), and in the California registry (1999 to 2003) non-Hispanic Black women with late-stage triple-negative disease had a five-year relative survival of 14 percent, the lowest of any group (Bauer 2007). United Kingdom: no UK registry publishes survival for the triple-negative subtype. For all breast cancer in England (women diagnosed 2018 to 2022) five-year net survival is almost 100 percent at stage 1, 90 percent at stage 2, around 75 percent at stage 3 and more than 30 percent at stage 4 (Cancer Research UK, from NHS England), and 76.6 percent of UK women survive ten years or more (2018). Subtype-specific UK figures come from cohorts: in the POSH study of women diagnosed at 40 or under (2000 to 2008), ten-year overall survival among 558 triple-negative patients was 72 percent in BRCA carriers and 69 percent in non-carriers (Copson 2018), and in a Manchester single-centre series of women aged 40 or under (2010 to 2015) five-year survival was 70.8 percent for triple-negative against 86.3 percent for ER-positive, HER2-negative tumours (Monaghan 2024). What moves the figures: stage at diagnosis above all; response to chemotherapy given before surgery, with ten-year relapse-free survival of 86 percent after a pathological complete response, 81 percent for residual cancer burden class I, 55 percent for class II and 23 percent for class III (Symmans 2017); and the newer regimens, with five-year overall survival of 86.6 percent for stage II and III disease treated with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy against 81.7 percent with chemotherapy alone in KEYNOTE-522 (Schmid 2024). Relapse risk is concentrated in the first three to five years and is low thereafter (Dent 2007).

records.name: Basal-like 1 triple-negative breast cancer (BL1)
aka: Cell-cycle and DNA damage response subtype of TNBC
records.tldr: Within triple-negative breast cancer, BL1 is a research RNA pattern linked to cell division and DNA-damage responses. It is different from a test showing failed DNA repair or benefit from a particular drug.
records.summary:
In Lehmann's 2011 analysis, BL1 was an expression cluster enriched for cell-cycle and DNA-damage-response programmes; representative cell models showed preferential cisplatin sensitivity. Enrichment for a response programme does not itself prove a functional repair defect. The 2016 TNBCtype-4 refinement retained BL1 as one of four tumour-focused profiles.

Across five historical neoadjuvant datasets, the 2016 report found pathological complete response in 41 percent of BL1 cases (95 percent confidence interval 33 to 51), 18 percent of BL2 (9 to 28) and 29 percent of LAR (17 to 41). Masuda's separate retrospective study included 146 profiled TNBCs, with 130 receiving standard neoadjuvant therapy and having evaluable response; BL1 had a 52 percent pCR rate there. These datasets do not supply a universal response probability.

The exploratory GeparSixto HRD analysis used its own definition, HRD score at least 42 and/or tumour BRCA mutation, measured successfully in 193 of 315 TNBC participants. In that HR-deficient subset pCR was 63.5 percent with carboplatin versus 33.9 percent without. The treatment-by-HRD interaction was not significant (p=0.327); the report concluded that HRD did not predict extra carboplatin benefit. This was not a validation of a BL1 call as a treatment-selection test.

A research expression label, a receptor-test classification, a histological type and an inherited-risk result describe different observations. Keep the specimen, classifier/version, preprocessing, reference data and uncertainty. A label or pathway-enrichment pattern alone does not establish functional dependence or benefit from a particular treatment.

Keep BL1, functional HR repair, a BRCA result, an HRD score and trial-specific predictive evidence separate.

Burstein's BLIA and BLIS are immune-associated groups in a separate classifier. They are not established child subtypes assigned by a Lehmann BL1 call.

records.name: Mesenchymal stem-like triple-negative breast cancer (MSL)
records.tldr: Within triple-negative breast cancer, MSL is a historical RNA label with a substantial stromal contribution. TNBCtype-4 reassigned these cases using expression correlations; it did not automatically turn every MSL call into mesenchymal cancer.
records.summary:
The 2011 TNBCtype system included a mesenchymal stem-like profile with lower proliferation-related expression and mesenchymal/stem-like programmes. In the 2016 study, paired laser-capture analyses of epithelial-enriched and stromal regions showed a strong stromal contribution to this signal.

TNBCtype-4 removed IM and MSL as separate tumour-focused labels and reassigned those samples to their second-highest correlated tumour-profile centroid. MSL was not simply renamed M, and a whole-tissue call does not prove that only stromal cells contributed. Immune and stromal signals remain useful context. Claudin-low is another phenotype with its own classifier and cannot be inferred from an MSL name alone.

A research expression label, a receptor-test classification, a histological type and an inherited-risk result describe different observations. Keep the specimen, classifier/version, preprocessing, reference data and uncertainty. A label or pathway-enrichment pattern alone does not establish functional dependence or benefit from a particular treatment.

An apparent change between a whole-tissue result and an enriched preparation can reflect mixture and processing. Compare specimen, method and scores before inferring tumour evolution.

records.tldr: TNBC RNA subtyping compares gene-expression patterns under a named research classifier. Tissue mixture, method and version matter, and the result is separate from receptor tests or a treatment choice.
records.summary:
Lehmann's original TNBCtype system described six expression groups: BL1, BL2, IM, M, MSL and LAR. The 2016 TNBCtype-4 refinement retained BL1, BL2, M and LAR as tumour-focused profiles after evaluating immune and stromal contributions to the IM and MSL signals. Removed-profile samples were reassigned to their second-highest correlated tumour-profile centroid, not automatically to M.

BL1 is associated with cell-cycle/DNA-damage-response programmes; BL2 with growth-factor and myoepithelial-associated expression; M with motility and differentiation; and LAR with luminal and androgen-related transcription. These are classifier associations, not proof of one cause, functional repair deficiency or dependence on an inhibitor.

The defining cell-model and retrospective chemotherapy studies generated treatment hypotheses. records.name: Pathologic complete response (pCR)
records.tldr: Pathological complete response records the absence of specified residual cancer in tissue after preoperative treatment. The specimen and response definition must accompany the result.
records.summary: In breast cancer, pCR must retain its named definition and specimens. FDA trial guidance describes two combined breast-and-sampled-node endpoints after neoadjuvant treatment: one permits residual ductal carcinoma in situ and the other excludes it. Older studies have also used breast-only definitions, so their response rates cannot be assumed to describe the combined endpoint. Response in sampled tissue, margin status, imaging, blood tests and long-term outcomes answer different questions.

notes: In FDA breast-trial guidance, ypT0/Tis ypN0 means no residual invasive cancer on haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) examination of the complete resected breast specimen and all sampled regional nodes after neoadjuvant systemic treatment. Residual DCIS is permitted. The stricter ypT0 ypN0 definition also excludes in situ cancer. Preserve the actual protocol and nodal assessment rules.

Breast-only clearance is not the combined breast-and-node endpoint. Residual invasive cancer in a sampled node prevents that combined pCR result even when breast invasion is absent or a blood assay is negative. A small negative biopsy, imaging response and negative circulating tumour DNA are different observations.

Residual DCIS can meet the invasive-clearance definition while still requiring separate margin assessment. In an otherwise qualifying specimen with DCIS but no breast invasion and no residual sampled-node cancer, the permissive definition is met and the stricter one is not. Neither pCR nor a negative local edge certifies cure or absence at every body site.

Cortazar and colleagues' CTNeoBC analysis pooled 11955 patients from 12 trials. In triple-negative disease, attaining ypT0/is ypN0 was associated with event-free-survival HR 0.24 and overall-survival HR 0.16 versus not attaining pCR. This patient-level association is not a guaranteed personal outcome. The 95% confidence intervals were 0.18 to 0.33 for the triple-negative EFS association and 0.11 to 0.25 for OS.

Trial-level increases in pCR had little association with event-free or overall-survival effects in CTNeoBC (R squared 0.03 and 0.24 respectively). The analysis could not validate pCR as a surrogate for improved long-term outcomes. A study reporting a pCR gain without mature survival comparison cannot infer the size of a survival benefit from the responder association.

FDA's July 2020 revision 1 guidance concerns pCR endpoints for trial design and accelerated approval in high-risk early-stage breast cancer. It is not an individual treatment or cure rule. In the notation, y denotes assessment after neoadjuvant treatment and p denotes pathological assessment. Sections and stains consume finite tissue; incomplete sampling, unexamined nodes and mixed endpoint definitions can invalidate comparisons.

KEYNOTE-522 separately demonstrated endpoint and survival results for the whole perioperative regimen in previously untreated stage II or III TNBC. In the 2020 primary pCR analysis of the first 602 randomised participants, pembrolizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy yielded 64.8% pCR versus 51.2% with placebo plus chemotherapy (difference 13.6 percentage points, 95% CI 5.4 to 21.8). The final 2024 overall-survival report covered all 1,174 randomised participants, including postoperative pembrolizumab or placebo: at 60 months, overall survival was 86.6% versus 81.7% (P = 0.002; median follow-up 75.1 months). Survival was measured directly; the pCR gain did not mathematically predict it or isolate which perioperative component produced the benefit.

In fictional case A, no breast invasion, residual DCIS and no residual cancer in sampled nodes meet ypT0/Tis ypN0 but not ypT0 ypN0. In fictional case B, the same breast finding plus a 4-mm residual invasive nodal deposit meets neither combined endpoint. Identical DCIS-at-ink findings in either case remain a separate margin question.

Subtract within the same endpoint and analysis: 64.8 minus 51.2 gives a 13.6-percentage-point pCR difference in the first 602 participants; 86.6 minus 81.7 gives 4.9 points in the separately reported 60-month survival estimates for all 1,174. The latter is often rounded to about five more people alive per hundred under the trial comparison. These time-to-event estimates are not literal counts from a complete hundred-person group, an individual forecast or a conversion from the pCR difference.

Triple-negative disease is where pathological complete response means most: in the CTNeoBC pooled analysis of 11,955 patients, eradication of tumour from breast and nodes (ypT0/is ypN0) was associated with event-free survival hazard ratio 0.24 and overall survival 0.16 in triple-negative disease, the strongest association of any subtype, yet trial-level increases in the rate did not predict survival gains (Cortazar 2014).

Triple-negative patients reach a complete response more often than others (22 against 11 percent in the MD Anderson series, 1985 to 2004) and then have similar survival, while those with residual disease do worse, particularly in the first three years (Liedtke 2008). Adding pembrolizumab to platinum chemotherapy raised the rate from 51.2 to 64.8 percent in KEYNOTE-522 (Schmid 2020).

records.name: Residual cancer burden (RCB)
records.tldr: Residual cancer burden combines breast and regional-node pathology measurements after preoperative chemotherapy into a continuous score and four response classes.
records.summary:
Residual cancer burden (RCB) combines measurements from the treated breast tumour bed and regional lymph nodes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The continuous index and its four classes are different outputs: RCB-0, RCB-I, RCB-II and RCB-III. It is not an anatomical stage or a percentage recurrence risk.

The six inputs are two residual tumour-bed dimensions in millimetres, overall cancer cellularity, the percentage of that cancer that is in situ, the positive-node count and the largest nodal metastasis diameter in millimetres. Overall cellularity uses tumour-bed area as its denominator; the in situ percentage uses the cancer component. In a fictional 100-unit bed with 20 units of cancer, of which 25% is in situ, invasive cancer occupies 15 units: 20 × (1 - 0.25). The 25% in situ input is fictional denominator teaching outside the MD Anderson protocol's listed nearest-10% estimates with low 1% and 5% choices. These are area fractions, not counted-cell fractions or sequencing purity.

Microscopic examination can revise the bed dimensions initially estimated at gross examination. Cellularity is averaged across the defined bed rather than taken only from the densest focus. A sparse breast bed cannot establish the nodal inputs, final margins or distant-disease status. The original study evaluated 382 patients in two chemotherapy cohorts and found prognostic information in the combined index. An association with later outcomes does not establish the benefit of a proposed additional treatment or supply an individual forecast.

notes: RCB combines six post-treatment pathology inputs: two breast-bed dimensions in millimetres, overall cancer area percentage, in situ percentage of the cancer component, positive-node count and largest nodal metastasis diameter in millimetres. Distinguish continuous index from classes 0, I, II and III, and both from ypTNM stage or recurrence percentages.

CAP 4.11 describes the RCB breast span as the two-dimensional extent of residual invasive carcinoma, excluding DCIS from the span. The MD Anderson microscopy protocol instead starts with the gross tumour bed, revises its boundaries microscopically and estimates invasive plus in situ cancer area in that bed, using the largest bed for multicentric disease. State the protocol and denominator rather than merging these wordings. The largest contiguous residual invasive focus without adjacent treatment fibrosis supplies ypT; the gross scar, that focus and an RCB bed are different measurements.

RCB nodal measurement includes intervening treatment-related fibrosis and extranodal extension within the residual metastatic area, whereas ypN uses the largest contiguous residual focus without that fibrosis. Separate deposits divided by normal nodal tissue remain separate. Routine-stain ITC-only nodes enter RCB calculations although they are excluded from the AJCC positive-node count. Do not move a nodal number between these methods without its definition.

CAP states that RCB was not designed or validated for neoadjuvant endocrine treatment and advises against reporting its score or class there. Individual measurements such as cellularity may still describe residual disease. Use the official pathology assessment and calculator for unusual findings; low breast cellularity alone cannot establish nodal clearance or pCR.

Yau and colleagues pooled 5161 chemotherapy-treated stage I to III patients from 12 institutes and trials. Across receptor subtypes, the unadjusted event hazard ratio per RCB unit ranged from 1.55 to 2.16. The adjusted range was 1.52 to 2.09. In the complete-covariate triple-negative model (1585 patients), the adjusted HR was 1.93 (95% CI 1.74 to 2.13). Adjustment included age and baseline T category, nodal status and grade; these are prognostic associations, not treatment-benefit estimates.

For a fictional 20 by 10 mm bed, 20% overall cancer cellularity, 50% in situ share of cancer, two positive nodes and a 3-mm largest nodal metastasis, d_prim is 14.1421356 mm and f_inv is 0.10. The breast term is 1.4849628 and nodal term 1.3256445, summing to 2.8106074, approximately 2.811 and RCB-II. With zero involved nodes the nodal term is zero and the breast term remains approximately 1.485, also RCB-II. This is not stage II or a recurrence percentage; the separate 25% in situ denominator illustration is not this specimen.

RCB classes use the continuous index without rounding at a boundary: 0 is RCB-0; greater than 0 through 1.36 is RCB-I; greater than 1.36 through 3.28 is RCB-II; and greater than 3.28 is RCB-III. The NCI BOLD data elements record these cutoffs. Residual in situ disease can be compatible with RCB-0 under the method; use the specified nodal and pathological assessment rather than equating any ypN0 modifier with complete response.

Symmans and colleagues' 2007 typeset equation defines d_prim = sqrt(d1 × d2), f_inv = (C/100) × (1 - S/100), and RCB = 1.4 × (f_inv × d_prim)^0.17 + [4 × (1 - 0.75^N) × d_met]^0.17. The entire nodal bracket is raised to 0.17. Here N originally counts involved axillary nodes and d_met is the largest axillary metastasis diameter. Because only the largest deposit was measured, the model assumed each additional metastasis had 75% of the diameter of the next largest. Preserve full precision near class boundaries.

The 2007 study derived the index in 241 patients treated with paclitaxel followed by fluorouracil, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide, and validated it in 141 treated with the latter combination: 382 patients with T1 to T3, N0 to N1, M0 disease. Class boundaries here come from NCI BOLD data elements, not the equation itself. This empirically fitted prognostic index is neither a cell count nor a personal probability.

Use the official calculator with the pathology team's protocol-specific assessment for unusual findings; low breast cellularity cannot establish negative nodes. A per-unit hazard ratio compares event rates under a study model, not a recurrence percentage or an estimate of benefit from adding treatment.

In triple-negative disease the residual cancer burden classes separate long-term risk sharply: ten-year relapse-free survival was 86 percent after a pathological complete response, 81 percent for RCB-I, 55 percent for RCB-II and 23 percent for RCB-III in the paclitaxel then FAC cohorts (Symmans 2017), which is why RCB-II and III residual disease is the setting for adjuvant escalation trials.
RCB 0 or I was the response endpoint that homologous recombination deficiency predicted in three neoadjuvant platinum trials (Telli 2016).

The staging manual now asks for it. The ninth edition of UICC TNM, recommended from 1 January 2026, clarifies that the ypT category must be based on the largest continuous focus of residual invasive cancer, excluding treatment-related fibrosis, with multiple foci carrying the m suffix, and recommends that the pathology report add an estimate of the extent of residual disease by the residual cancer burden method (Brierley 2026). Residual cancer burden is therefore no longer only a trial endpoint; it is what the stage cannot express.

records.name: Tumour-bed cellularity
records.tldr: Tumour-bed cellularity estimates cancer-occupied area within a defined treated breast bed. The in situ share uses a different denominator.
records.summary: Label the region, numerator and denominator before interpreting cellularity. Overall cancer area and the in situ share of that cancer are separate RCB inputs, neither interchangeable with sequencing purity or a score by itself.

notes: For RCB, overall cancer cellularity estimates the area occupied by invasive plus in situ cancer within a defined residual breast bed. The in situ percentage instead uses the cancer component as denominator. Microscopic review can revise bed boundaries and should represent sparse as well as dense regions; selecting only a dense focus changes the measurement.

Invasive bed fraction equals overall cancer fraction multiplied by one minus the in situ fraction of cancer. In a fictional 100-unit bed with 20 units of cancer, 25% in situ means 5 bed units in situ and 15 invasive. The invasive share is 75% of cancer but only 15% of the whole bed. These idealised area units teach denominators, not counting instructions or the precision of a clinical estimate.

Area occupied by cancer, the proportion of counted cells that are malignant and the fraction of sequenced DNA contributed by cancer have different denominators. A selected assay block may also differ from the whole residual bed. Do not enter an area-cellularity estimate as sequencing purity or describe 25% of cancer as 25% of the bed.

Retain the named bed, specimen, treatment setting, mapping and representative sections, overall area percentage and in situ share separately. Incomplete sampling, a misdefined bed and heterogeneous distribution can bias the estimate; staining or sampling consumes finite tissue. There is no universal low/high cellularity cutoff that alone selects treatment.

Cellularity alone supplies neither nodal burden, final margins, distant status, pCR nor an RCB score. CAP's residual-invasive RCB span excludes DCIS, while the MD Anderson protocol estimates invasive plus in situ area in a microscopically revised cancer bed. Neither is interchangeable with the largest contiguous ypT focus. CAP advises against RCB score/class after neoadjuvant endocrine therapy, although individual residual measurements may still be useful.

The MD Anderson protocol estimates overall cellularity and in situ percentage to the nearest 10%, with additional 1% and 5% choices for low values. The 25% in situ example above is fictional denominator arithmetic outside those listed estimation increments. Its arithmetic remains 20 × 0.25 = 5 in situ and 20 - 5 = 15 invasive bed units. A separate protocol-aligned 20% in situ illustration would give 4 in situ and 16 invasive units. Neither should be confused with the RCB example using 50% in situ.

Two fictional treated breast beds can have the same dimensions while one contains sparse residual carcinoma and the other dense residual carcinoma. The footprint alone cannot distinguish their viable cancer area. Read overall cancer area and the in situ share of that cancer with their different denominators, then keep regional nodes and final margins separate. A DCIS-permitting breast-and-node pCR definition can be met when DCIS remains at an involved final edge but no residual invasive breast or nodal cancer is found. Add an involved regional node and that combined endpoint is no longer met, even with a negative blood assay; this does not by itself establish distant spread.

records.name: Sentinel node biopsy
records.tldr: Sentinel-node biopsy identifies and examines selected draining nodes. Its result describes that sampling procedure, with limits that depend on the disease and treatment setting.
records.summary:
A dye, radiotracer or other mapping agent identifies draining nodes for removal and pathological examination. Sentinel sampling and broader nodal dissection provide different amounts of tissue and have different risks. Neither a negative sampled node nor the operation name establishes the status of every regional node or distant organ.

The NCI fact sheet describes a radioactive tracer, blue dye or both for mapping. It identifies breast cancer and melanoma as the most common uses and notes use or investigation in other cancers, including endometrial, penile, vulvar, cervical and head-and-neck disease. records.name: Targeted axillary dissection
records.tldr: Targeted axillary dissection combines sentinel-node sampling with removal of a previously marked node. Marker recovery and the pathological result need their own documentation.
records.summary:
In the studied post-neoadjuvant setting, a node with biopsy-confirmed metastasis is marked before treatment and localised for removal alongside mapped sentinel nodes. The marked node may not be a sentinel node. Caudle and colleagues reported a 2.0% false-negative rate (1 of 50 patients with residual disease) for targeted dissection followed by the full axillary reference procedure. This result depends on the population, technique and reference assessment and is not a guarantee for every patient or centre.

Localisation approaches include an iodine-125 seed, magnetic seed, carbon tattoo, wire-guided localisation and radiofrequency-based tags. The IMTAD primary study compared the first three; its discussion describes separate feasibility reports for wire and radiofrequency approaches, not a head-to-head comparison of every method. Carbon is detected visually, whereas the iodine and magnetic seeds are probe-detected. Mapping technique, marker recovery and examined-node number need to be documented rather than assuming identical performance across methods.

Subsequent surgery and regional irradiation are separate questions. In NSABP B-51, patients with biopsy-proven cT1 to T3, cN1, M0 disease who reached ypN0 after neoadjuvant chemotherapy were randomised to regional nodal irradiation or its omission. Irradiation did not significantly improve the primary invasive breast cancer recurrence-free interval at the reported follow-up; this is not proof of no benefit in every setting. ATNEC separately studies axillary management after neoadjuvant chemotherapy; its registry lists recruiting, last updated 30 March 2026.

These overlapping study analyses have different denominators and do not guarantee performance in every setting.

records.name: Resection margins (R0 / R1 / R2)
records.tldr: Resection margins describe the assessed boundaries of removed tissue. A clear local boundary is not proof that no cancer exists elsewhere, and interpretation depends on the organ and reporting standard.
records.summary:
Margin assessment examines the cut boundaries of a submitted specimen and any additional margins. The operative account, sampled pathology and final residual-disease classification are connected but different observations. In the traditional R classification, R0 means no residual tumour under the applied assessment, R1 microscopic residual tumour and R2 gross residual tumour. These categories do not establish absence of every unseen cancer cell.

Definitions and required margin distances can vary by organ, disease and jurisdiction. The 2024 IASLC proposal describes an additional lung-cancer category for uncertain residual status. A clear microscopic edge is therefore not interchangeable with every definition of complete resection. Use the relevant report and standard rather than transferring a breast or pancreatic convention to every cancer.

An old main-specimen edge may cease to be the final edge when an additional oriented strip is removed; if their relationship is unclear, preserve uncertainty and request surgical correlation.

Its evidence base excluded neoadjuvant therapy and pure DCIS. The 2016 pure-DCIS consensus supported a 2-mm adequate-margin standard with whole-breast irradiation; a narrower negative margin alone was not an indication for mastectomy. Conversely, invasive cancer at the confirmed outer edge of an additional lateral specimen remains a local margin finding even if a blood assay is negative.

The lymph-node capsule, a vessel lumen and a surgical cut edge are different boundaries. Margin status does not diagnose distant metastasis or whole-body clearance; completion excision, mastectomy and axillary surgery address different tissues.

A margin is a cut boundary of removed tissue. Pathology assesses sampled sections of that local boundary: a positive final margin means cancer reaches the evaluated cut edge. Sampling, sectioning and staining consume finite tissue, and cannot examine every possible cell. No ink on tumour does not mean no cancer anywhere in the person.

Pancreatic cancer uses a 1 mm rule: tumour within 1 mm of a margin is R1 (Royal College of Pathologists), which makes 76 to 85 percent of standardised head resections R1; the pancreatic glossary term carries the series and the ESPAC-3 survival by margin (Ghaneh 2019).

records.tldr: Treatment effect describes tissue changes after therapy, assessed separately from whether viable cancer remains in the examined breast and nodes.
records.summary: Response-related changes and residual carcinoma answer different questions. Interpretation needs treatment history, mapped sampling and separate breast and nodal findings. Fibrosis is not automatically residual tumour size or proof of complete response.

notes: After preoperative therapy, fibrosis, necrosis, inflammation and histiocytic aggregates can be response-related tissue changes. Residual viable carcinoma is a separate morphological assessment, not a culture test of every cell. Response changes and residual cancer can coexist; scarring alone does not establish that no cancer remains. Fibrosis means collagen-rich scarring, necrosis means dead tissue and histiocytes are tissue macrophages.

CAP 4.11 describes the RCB breast span as the two-dimensional extent of residual invasive carcinoma, excluding DCIS from the span. The MD Anderson microscopy protocol instead starts with the gross tumour bed, revises its boundaries microscopically and estimates invasive plus in situ cancer area in that bed, using the largest bed for multicentric disease. State the protocol and denominator rather than merging these wordings. The largest contiguous residual invasive focus without adjacent treatment fibrosis supplies ypT; the gross scar, that focus and an RCB bed are different measurements. For ypN, adjacent treatment fibrosis is likewise excluded from the contiguous staging dimension; RCB nodal measurement has its own rule.

Assessment connects pretreatment location, imaging or marker information, gross mapping, a sampling plan and microscopy. Sparse, scattered residual foci make arbitrary-section interpretation unreliable. A broad scar can contain residual invasive cancer without the whole scar being solid cancer.

Breast and node response are reported separately. Nodal scarring or histiocytic aggregates without residual cancer can be consistent with prior treated involvement, but do not independently establish biopsy-proven baseline metastasis. Prior biopsy or other injury can also produce repair changes; a scar alone cannot establish a drug-specific effect.

RCB is not validated for neoadjuvant endocrine treatment; CAP advises against reporting a score/class in that setting even when individual residual measurements are recorded. Combined pCR requires its stated breast-and-node definition and appropriate specimens, may permit DCIS and does not establish whole-body eradication. Preserve the pretreatment record alongside residual findings.

records.name: Lines of therapy
records.tldr: A line of therapy is a treatment strategy counted within a specified disease setting. First-line means the initial strategy in that setting; it does not mean the first medicine a person has ever received.
records.summary:
Lines of therapy describe successive treatment strategies under a clinical record or study's stated counting rule. First-line is the initial strategy for the specified disease setting. A later strategy may follow because treatment does not work, stops working or causes intolerable harm. The setting and reason for change belong beside the number.

In an advanced-cancer trial, first-line can mean no earlier systemic treatment for advanced disease, while previous treatment around surgery remains part of the exposure history and eligibility assessment. Several medicines, repeating cycles and planned blocks can belong to one strategy. A line count does not measure remaining life or establish that treatment options are exhausted.

A planned switch between blocks differs from changing strategy after progression. Neoadjuvant and adjuvant describe roles around the main treatment, rather than first and second line.

Keep four entries together: disease setting, strategy with start and stop dates, reason for change, and the counting convention. Maintenance, a pause, dose reduction or removal of one component must be interpreted under that convention. A database algorithm can draw boundaries differently from the clinical account, so preserve the actual events before assigning a number.

Those descriptions are compatible: prior early-disease treatment and prior advanced-disease treatment are different variables. The example explains the study population, not a current prescribing choice.

In a fictional history, combination A precedes definitive surgery and medicine B follows it as part of one planned early-disease strategy. Years later, the first systemic strategy for metastatic disease is first-line metastatic under the stated rule of no earlier systemic metastatic treatment. A and B remain in the exposure history. The setting boundary changes what is being counted; it is not a universal rule for every switch or maintenance phase.

Before comparing studies labelled first-line or later-line, check prior exposure, eligibility, resistance history, tolerability and the comparator. Matching a drug name does not match the populations. To explain a line number, name the disease setting, earlier strategy and counting rule, rather than turning that history label into an individual forecast.

records.name: De-escalation, escalation and response-adapted therapy
records.tldr: Response-adapted treatment uses a defined assessment to guide a planned next step. Continuing, reducing, changing or adding treatment each needs evidence for that strategy and its harms.
records.summary:
A response-adapted strategy specifies the population, what is measured, the assessment time, the result that triggers a branch and what happens next. It can continue treatment, switch medicines, add treatment or omit a component. The aim and evidence must be stated for the actual branch; adaptation is not a synonym for less treatment.

A prognostic result can identify risk without proving that changing treatment on its basis improves outcomes. An omission strategy must assess the outcomes and harms of that decision in the relevant population. Noninferiority is one possible design requiring a justified margin, rather than an automatic property of every adaptation study. KEYNOTE-522 compared whole assigned strategies and did not reserve its postoperative phase for residual disease or independently randomise escalation at surgery.

Predicted pathological complete response is not the surgical finding itself, and a negative biopsy describes only the tissue submitted. A baseline marker selecting a medicine differs from an on-treatment response rule. Response adaptation changes a participant's later treatment; response-adaptive randomisation changes assignment probabilities for future participants. A trial can use both. A safety-driven hold or substitution is a further distinct decision: favourable cancer response does not settle whether treatment can safely continue, or prove a changed course equivalent to the original one.

records.name: Anthracyclines (doxorubicin, epirubicin)
records.tldr: Anthracyclines are chemotherapy medicines that disturb DNA and an enzyme that cuts and reseals it. They can also harm the heart, including after treatment, so prior exposure and heart function matter.
records.summary:
Doxorubicin and epirubicin are members of the anthracycline family. Doxorubicin intercalates between DNA bases and can stabilise complexes of DNA with topoisomerase II, an enzyme that temporarily cuts both DNA strands, passes another segment and reseals the cut. Stabilising this intermediate interferes with resealing; it differs from simply switching the enzyme off. Other interactions, including reactive molecules and cell membranes, also contribute.

Cardiac risk depends on cumulative exposure, prior anthracyclines, other treatments and the person’s circumstances. It is not defined by a single dose above which every person develops cardiomyopathy or below which nobody does. A normal baseline heart scan and a symptom-free infusion cannot guarantee freedom from later cardiac injury.

These are different mechanisms; their names alone do not establish cross-resistance or a useful next treatment. The antitumour-antibiotic classification refers to the drug family and origin; it does not make an anthracycline cancer regimen routine treatment for an infection.

The 2019 conventional doxorubicin US label describes cardiomyopathy during treatment or years later and asks that prior anthracycline or anthracenedione doses count towards cumulative exposure. For administration every three weeks, its estimates range from 1% to 2% at 300 mg/m² cumulative doxorubicin to 6% to 20% at 500 mg/m². The same label reports secondary acute myeloid leukaemia or myelodysplastic syndromes, with cumulative incidences from 0.2% at five years to 1.5% at ten years in two adjuvant breast-cancer trials.

Dose per administration and lifetime cumulative amount are separate quantities, often expressed in milligrams per square metre. Left ventricular ejection fraction measures cardiac pumping function; it is neither a tumour-response test nor a guarantee against future injury. Conventional and liposomal formulations need their own instructions and evidence. In a fictional experiment, a strand-break marker plus a normal baseline heart scan establishes neither successful cancer treatment nor absence of cardiac risk.

records.name: Regimen and cycles
records.tldr: A chemotherapy regimen specifies the medicines, amounts and timing. A cycle is a defined period of treatment and recovery, whose duration and supportive care depend on the plan.
records.summary:
A chemotherapy regimen specifies the medicines, formulations, amounts, administration days, intervals, number of cycles and supportive care. A cycle is a defined period of treatment and recovery. Abbreviations such as AC, EC, TC, FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, FOLFIRINOX, CAPOX and BEP name particular combinations; a treatment abbreviation alone does not supply every dose or eligibility condition.

Dose-dense scheduling shortens intervals relative to a stated reference. Some tested regimens use growth-factor support, but that is a property of the protocol, not a rule supplied by the word dose-dense. Compare the intended schedule with what was delivered, and distinguish the duration of one phase from that of the whole treatment course.

Read a combined plan with six entries: disease setting and goal, each medicine's mechanism, the studied population and comparator, route and cadence with sequence, risks with monitoring and supportive care, and the separate local-treatment question. This is a reading aid rather than orders or consent. A laboratory rationale for adding a pathway inhibitor fills the mechanism entry but does not supply the remaining clinical evidence, delivery or safety entries.

The KEYNOTE-522 card concerns previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer and a whole preoperative and postoperative strategy. Four three-week cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin preceded four with an anthracycline and cyclophosphamide, followed by surgery and up to nine assigned pembrolizumab or placebo cycles. The planned blocks span about 12, 12 and 27 dosing weeks: eight plus nine gives up to 17 assigned doses, approximately a year, with the surgical gap and holds affecting the actual calendar. Its first-602 pCR result, all-1,174 survival analyses and treatment-related safety results have distinct denominators and cutoffs. Radiation indications and the actual breast and node procedures require their own entries. The trial calendar is not a personal administration record.

The mechanism entry also needs the right class. Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules used in cellular organisation, intracellular transport and division; carboplatin forms DNA cross-links; doxorubicin has DNA intercalation and topoisomerase-II-associated effects; cyclophosphamide is activated to alkylating metabolites. Pembrolizumab binds PD-1 on T cells and blocks interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, reducing that inhibitory signalling rather than strengthening every immune function. These are different jobs, not a demonstration that combining more mechanisms improves outcomes. Oral capecitabine is not made mild by its route, nor does its mechanism establish a benefit from adding it to every plan.

Dose is the amount given; dose intensity describes amount delivered per unit time. Dose-dense scheduling shortens intervals relative to a specified reference, while the therapeutic index concerns useful effect relative to harm. These distinctions do not prove that more frequent delivery always helps. Cancer activity does not imply uniform exposure or sensitivity throughout the body, and normal tissues can also be injured. External-beam radiation treats planned local volumes and can affect nearby healthy structures. Different mechanisms can bring overlapping harms, so a component's hold, substitution or continuation depends on the actual medicines, interactions and purpose rather than a diagram alone.

Give supportive care its own part of the record. Immune-related inflammation, including pneumonitis, needs clinical attribution; a symptom alone does not name its cause. A low neutrophil count and infection risk differ from the decision to use selected granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) support. Nausea differs from vomiting, and acute, delayed and anticipatory patterns need their timing recorded. Supportive medicines can improve tolerability without treating the cancer itself, and symptoms during a combination can have more than one possible cause.

In a fictional calendar, block A has four planned visits but only three administrations and one hold. Interim imaging was acquired before that visit was rescheduled; block B was substituted after safety review; surgery has its own operation and specimen-collection dates. The scan reflects its acquisition date and the record shows changed exposure. It does not prove that a delay caused an outcome or that the substituted course preserved exactly the original benefit. Six planned doses with five documented administrations and a cancelled visit likewise establish five administrations, not six.

Systemic medicines, breast surgery and radiation can contribute different jobs to one goal. Systemic reach does not guarantee activity in every cancer cell, and local treatment is not a ranking of importance. The breast operation and node assessment are separate procedures. Receptor classification alone does not supply stage, earlier exposure, eligibility or safety. To assess a fictional claim that three mechanisms make a combination better, ask for the population, comparator, outcome, follow-up, actual delivery and harms. Neither the intensity nor the number of medicines by itself establishes curative intent.

records.tldr: KEYNOTE-522 compared adding pembrolizumab before and after surgery with placebo on the same chemotherapy and surgery sequence in early triple-negative breast cancer. It measured improvements in response and survival.
